```{r load data for shannon }

# ================================================================
# STEP 1: READ AND COMBINE BIOLOGICAL DATA
# ================================================================

# Read both sheets (2024 and 2023 data)
bio_2024 <- read_excel("Bio_WormsDone.xlsx", sheet = "Bio_RealNames_Worms2024")
bio_2023 <- read_excel("Bio_WormsDone.xlsx", sheet = "2023")

# Add a Year column to track which year each sample is from
bio_2024$Year <- 2024
bio_2023$Year <- 2023

# Combine both years - keep only the columns that exist in both sheets
bio_data <- bind_rows(
  bio_2024 %>% select(Station, espece, Nb_individu, poids, Year, 
                      ScientificName_accepted),
  bio_2023 %>% select(Station, espece, Nb_individu, poids, Year) %>%
    mutate(ScientificName_accepted = espece)  # Use espece as scientific name for 2023
)

# Check the combined data
cat("Total rows after combining:", nrow(bio_data), "\n")
cat("Rows from 2024:", sum(bio_data$Year == 2024), "\n")
cat("Rows from 2023:", sum(bio_data$Year == 2023), "\n")

# ================================================================
# STEP 2: CLEAN THE DATA
# ================================================================

# Remove rows where Nb_individu is NA (these are fragments/pieces, not countable individuals)
cat("\nRows with NA abundance:", sum(is.na(bio_data$Nb_individu)), "\n")

bio_data_clean <- bio_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Nb_individu)) %>%  # Remove NA abundances
  filter(Nb_individu > 0)           # Keep only positive abundances

cat("Rows after removing NAs:", nrow(bio_data_clean), "\n")

# Check which stations we have
unique_stations <- unique(bio_data_clean$Station)
cat("\nNumber of unique stations:", length(unique_stations), "\n")

# ================================================================
# STEP 3: HANDLE DUPLICATES (if any)
# ================================================================

# Check for duplicate Station-Species combinations
duplicates <- bio_data_clean %>%
  group_by(Station, ScientificName_accepted) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n > 1)

if(nrow(duplicates) > 0) {
  cat("\nFound", nrow(duplicates), "duplicate Station-Species combinations\n")
  cat("Summing abundances for duplicates...\n")
  
  # Sum abundances for duplicates
  bio_data_clean <- bio_data_clean %>%
    group_by(Station, ScientificName_accepted, Year) %>%
    summarise(
      Nb_individu = sum(Nb_individu, na.rm = TRUE),
      poids = sum(poids, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
} else {
  cat("\nNo duplicates found - data is clean!\n")
}

# ================================================================
# STEP 4: CREATE COMMUNITY MATRIX (Station x Species)
# ================================================================

# Create wide format matrix for Shannon calculation
community_wide <- bio_data_clean %>%
  select(Station, ScientificName_accepted, Nb_individu) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = ScientificName_accepted,
    values_from = Nb_individu,
    values_fill = 0  # Fill missing with 0
  )

# Convert to matrix format for vegan
stations <- community_wide$Station
community_matrix <- as.data.frame(community_wide[, -1])
rownames(community_matrix) <- stations

# Check dimensions
cat("\nCommunity matrix dimensions:\n")
cat("Stations:", nrow(community_matrix), "\n")
cat("Species:", ncol(community_matrix), "\n")

# ================================================================
# STEP 5: CALCULATE SHANNON INDEX
# ================================================================

# Calculate Shannon diversity index
shannon_values <- diversity(community_matrix, index = "shannon")

# Calculate other useful metrics
richness <- specnumber(community_matrix)  # Number of species
total_abundance <- rowSums(community_matrix)  # Total individuals

# Create results dataframe
shannon_df <- data.frame(
  Station = names(shannon_values),
  Shannon_Index = as.numeric(shannon_values),
  Species_Richness = as.numeric(richness),
  Total_Abundance = as.numeric(total_abundance)
)

# Summary
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("SHANNON INDEX SUMMARY:\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Number of stations:", nrow(shannon_df), "\n")
cat("Mean Shannon Index:", round(mean(shannon_df$Shannon_Index), 3), "\n")
cat("Min Shannon Index:", round(min(shannon_df$Shannon_Index), 3), "\n")
cat("Max Shannon Index:", round(max(shannon_df$Shannon_Index), 3), "\n")
cat("Mean Species Richness:", round(mean(shannon_df$Species_Richness), 1), "\n")

# ================================================================
# STEP 6: READ COORDINATES
# ================================================================

coord_data <- read_excel("env.xlsx", sheet = "station done")

# Select and rename relevant columns
coord_data <- coord_data %>%
  select(
    Station,
    Latitude = lat,
    Longitude = long,
    Sector = secteur,
    Depth,
    Chla,
    Phaeo
  )

cat("\nCoordinate data loaded:", nrow(coord_data), "stations\n")

# ================================================================
# STEP 7: ADD YEAR INFORMATION
# ================================================================

# Get year for each station from bio_data
station_years <- bio_data_clean %>%
  select(Station, Year) %>%
  distinct()

# Some stations might have data from both years - take the most common year
station_years <- station_years %>%
  group_by(Station) %>%
  summarise(Year = max(Year), .groups = "drop")  # Take most recent year if duplicates

# ================================================================
# STEP 8: MERGE EVERYTHING
# ================================================================

# Merge Shannon indices with coordinates
final_data <- shannon_df %>%
  left_join(coord_data, by = "Station") %>%
  left_join(station_years, by = "Station")

# Check for stations without coordinates
missing_coords <- final_data %>%
  filter(is.na(Longitude) | is.na(Latitude))

if(nrow(missing_coords) > 0) {
  cat("\nWARNING:", nrow(missing_coords), "stations missing coordinates:\n")
  print(missing_coords$Station)
  
  # Remove stations without coordinates
  final_data <- final_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(Longitude) & !is.na(Latitude))
}

cat("\nFinal dataset:", nrow(final_data), "stations with complete data\n")

# ================================================================
# STEP 9: CONVERT TO SPATIAL OBJECT
# ================================================================

# Create sf object (assuming coordinates are in WGS84 lat/lon)
benthic_sf <- st_as_sf(final_data, 
                       coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),
                       crs = 4326)  # WGS84

# Transform to UTM Zone 19N (appropriate for Saguenay)
benthic_sf <- st_transform(benthic_sf, crs = 32619)

# ================================================================
# STEP 10: SAVE YOUR RESULTS
# ================================================================

# Save as CSV (with coordinates as separate columns)
final_data_export <- final_data %>%
  arrange(Station)

write.csv(final_data_export, "benthic_data_complete.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Save as shapefile
st_write(benthic_sf, "benthic_stations.shp", delete_dsn = TRUE)

# Save as R object (fastest for later use)
saveRDS(benthic_sf, "benthic_data.rds")

# Also save the raw bio data for reference
write.csv(bio_data_clean, "bio_data_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nFiles saved:\n")
cat("- benthic_data_complete.csv\n")
cat("- benthic_stations.shp\n")
cat("- benthic_data.rds\n")
cat("- bio_data_clean.csv\n")

# ================================================================
# STEP 11: VISUALIZATIONS
# ================================================================

# 1. Histogram of Shannon Index
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

hist(final_data$Shannon_Index, 
     breaks = 20,
     col = "lightblue",
     main = "Distribution of Shannon Index",
     xlab = "Shannon Index")

# 2. Shannon vs Species Richness
plot(final_data$Species_Richness, final_data$Shannon_Index,
     pch = 16, col = "darkblue",
     xlab = "Species Richness",
     ylab = "Shannon Index",
     main = "Diversity Metrics")
abline(lm(Shannon_Index ~ Species_Richness, data = final_data), 
       col = "red", lwd = 2)

# 3. Shannon by Sector
if("Sector" %in% names(final_data)) {
  boxplot(Shannon_Index ~ Sector, data = final_data,
          col = "lightgreen",
          main = "Shannon Index by Sector",
          las = 2)
}

# 4. Shannon by Year
if("Year" %in% names(final_data)) {
  boxplot(Shannon_Index ~ Year, data = final_data,
          col = c("orange", "cyan"),
          main = "Shannon Index by Year")
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# 5. Spatial map
plot(benthic_sf["Shannon_Index"], 
     pch = 16, 
     cex = 2,
     main = "Shannon Index - Saguenay Fjord",
     key.pos = 4)

# ================================================================
# STEP 12: SUMMARY TABLE BY SECTOR
# ================================================================

if("Sector" %in% names(final_data)) {
  summary_by_sector <- final_data %>%
    group_by(Sector) %>%
    summarise(
      N_stations = n(),
      Mean_Shannon = round(mean(Shannon_Index), 3),
      SD_Shannon = round(sd(Shannon_Index), 3),
      Mean_Richness = round(mean(Species_Richness), 1),
      Mean_Abundance = round(mean(Total_Abundance), 0)
    )
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("SUMMARY BY SECTOR:\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(summary_by_sector)
}

# ================================================================
# STEP 13: SUMMARY TABLE BY YEAR
# ================================================================

if("Year" %in% names(final_data)) {
  summary_by_year <- final_data %>%
    group_by(Year) %>%
    summarise(
      N_stations = n(),
      Mean_Shannon = round(mean(Shannon_Index), 3),
      SD_Shannon = round(sd(Shannon_Index), 3),
      Mean_Richness = round(mean(Species_Richness), 1)
    )
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("SUMMARY BY YEAR:\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(summary_by_year)
}

# ================================================================
# FINAL DATA PREVIEW
# ================================================================

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("FINAL DATASET PREVIEW:\n")
cat("========================================\n")
print(head(final_data, 10))

cat("\nColumn names in final dataset:\n")
print(names(final_data))
```
